Zakat Calculator

This zakat calculator Pakistan Muslims can use before Ramadan or at their yearly Zakat date adds up your cash, gold, silver and other assets, deducts liabilities, checks the total against the government-notified nisab, and calculates 2.5% Zakat if nisab is reached.

🔒 Your files never leave your device.

Government-notified nisab for 1447 AH (Ramadan 2026): Rs 503,529 — based on 52.5 tola silver; editable.

How to use

  1. Add up your cash, bank balances, and the current value of gold and silver you own.
  2. Add other zakatable assets, subtract debts you must repay, and check the nisab figure.
  3. Press Calculate Zakat — if your net assets reach nisab, Zakat is 2.5% of the net amount.

How it works

Zakat is 2.5% (one-fortieth) of net zakatable wealth held for a full lunar year, payable when that wealth reaches the nisab — the value of 52.5 tola silver (or 7.5 tola gold). Personal items such as your home, car and household goods are not zakatable. The nisab field uses the Government-notified nisab for 1447 AH (Ramadan 2026): Rs 503,529, based on 52.5 tola silver, and stays editable for later years.

Worked example: Example: net assets of Rs 1,000,000 are above the Rs 503,529 nisab, so Zakat due = 2.5% × 1,000,000 = Rs 25,000.

Frequently asked questions

What is the nisab for Zakat in 2026?

The Government-notified nisab for 1447 AH (Ramadan 2026) is Rs 503,529, based on the value of 52.5 tola silver. If your net zakatable assets are below this, Zakat is not due.

How much Zakat is charged on cash and savings?

2.5% of the total net amount, once it reaches nisab and a lunar year has passed over it.

Is Zakat due on the house I live in and my car?

No. Your residence, personal car and household items are not zakatable. Zakat applies to cash, gold, silver, savings and trade goods beyond personal use.

Should I deduct my debts?

Yes — money you genuinely owe and must repay is deducted before checking nisab and calculating the 2.5%.

When should Zakat be paid?

Many people choose a fixed date in Ramadan each year. What matters is that a full lunar year (hawl) has passed over the wealth.
